questions.q: Why do restrictive diets usually fail?
a: They fight your appetite and cannot be sustained
They cost more than most families can afford
They require too much exercise to be safe
They work only for people with medical advice
questions.why: Lesson 1 says eating against your appetite is counterintuitive, so diets rarely last.

questions.q: What happens to your body during a restrictive diet?
a: It enters starvation mode and later overeats
It stops feeling hunger after the first week
It burns fat faster the longer you restrict
It becomes permanently unable to digest sugar
questions.why: Lesson 2 says cutting calories triggers starvation, which leads to overeating when willpower runs out.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest keeping a food journal for?
a: To spot your hunger patterns and best meal times
To count every calorie you consume precisely
To prove to others that you are dieting
To compare your portions with a friend's
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends rating hunger from one to ten before and after meals to find patterns.

questions.q: How should you think about food, according to the book?
a: As fuel, not as something moral or forbidden
As a reward for exercise and discipline
As a treat to be earned through restraint
As medicine that must be measured carefully
questions.why: Lesson 3 says splitting food into good and bad categories leads to bingeing.

questions.q: What alternative does the summary suggest for cravings?
a: Try fruit or a nutritious substitute instead
Ignore the craving until it disappears
Eat a larger portion of the same treat
Replace meals with a protein shake
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests swapping cravings for a side of fruit or a nourishing alternative.
